verses.translation: Then, when Yeshua realized that the Perushim realized that Yeshua made talmidim and immersed more than Yochanan 2 (although Yeshua did not immerse – only his talmidim did), 3 they left Yehudah and went to Gelilah again.

(And he had to pass through Shomron.)2 5 So Yeshua came into a part of Shomron which is called Suchar,4 near the place which Ya’aqov gave to Yoseph his son – 6 and the spring of Ya’aqov was there. So Yeshua, being weary because of the way, sat by the spring. (And it was about the sixth hour of the day.)
Then a woman came to draw waters,7 so Yeshua said to her, “Give me some water to drink.”
(Now his talmidim went into the city to buy some food.)

Then that Shomronit woman said to him, “You who are a Yehudi,9 do you ask of me to give you water to drink while I am a woman from the place of Shomron?!” (For the Yehudim do not [hold company] with the Shomronim.)1 1 Yeshua answered and said to her, “If you had known the gift of El, and who he is who asks 1 In Hebrew a verb is often written only once in a sentence, but again implied a second time in remaining part of the sentence, called ‘verb gapping.’ This verb is probably implied here from the first part of the verse. 2 Hebrew name for the land of ‘Samaria.’ 3 Although Shomron was originally the name of a city, it was later used to refer to the regions around Shomron (Samaria). 4 Hebrew name for ‘Sychar.’ 5 Hebrew name for ‘Jacob.’ 6 Or “fountain.” 7 Water is always plural in Hebrew. 8 Hebrew word for a ‘Samarian’ woman. 9 Hebrew word for ‘Jew.’
Hebrew word for ‘Samarians.’ water to drink – you, you would perhaps ask him, and he would give you living waters!”
The woman answered him, “The well is deep, and you do not have something with which you can draw water; so how can you give me living water?
Are you greater than Ya’aqov our father, who gave this well to us – and he drank from this well, and his sons and his cattle?”

Yeshua answered and said to her, “Whosoever drinks of this water will have thirst again; 1 but whosoever drinks of the waters that I will give him will not thirst in eternity; but the waters that I give him will become a spring, leaping with everlasting life.”

So the woman said unto him, “Give me those waters, so that I will not have thirst and that I will not have to come here to draw waters in eternity.”5 1 Then Yeshua said to her, “Go and call your husband, and return here.”

The woman answered and said to him, “I do not have a husband.” So Yeshua said to her, “Truth you say that you do not have a husband, 1 for you had five husbands, but this one whom you have now is not your husband. Truth you speak.”
Then the woman said to him, “Adon,7 I realize that you are a prophet.

Our fathers prayed 1 Sarcasm; meaning ‘certainly / definitely.’ 2 Or “that he should give.” 3 Or “children” – Hebrew masculine includes feminine. 4 Or “into.” 5 Or “that I will never have to come here to draw water.” 6 Introductory imperative – idiom for saying it should happen immediately. Compare chapter 8:11. 7 Hebrew word for ‘Master.’ to YHWH in this mountain, but you say that the place where everyone has to pray to El is in Yerushalayim.”
So Yeshua said to the woman, “Believe me that a time will yet come, that you will not worship the Father on this mountain, nor in Yerushalayim.
You pray to whom you do not know; but we pray to whom we know – for shalom is about to come for the Yehudim.

But a time will come, and is now, that the true worshippers will worship the Father in Ruach and in truth, for the Father asks them that they worship according to these.5 2 El is Ruach, and those who pray to him – it is required that they pray to him in Ruach and in truth.”
So the woman said to him, “I know that Mashiach ( )6 is ready to come, and when he comes he will reveal many things to us.”
Then Yeshua said to her, “I am he – he who speaks with you!”

And right then his talmidim came, and they were astonished when they found him speaking with the woman. However, none of them asked him what he was speaking to her, such as, “What do you seek?” or, “What do you speak with her?”

So the woman left her house,8 and went to the city and said to the people, 2 “Come, and see! – A certain man made known to me 1 Plural in Hebrew, referring to the Jews. 2 Plural in Hebrew. 3 Or possibly ‘salvation.’ 4 Or “the Father seeks those who.” 5 “These” (feminine plural) refers back to Ruach and Truth. 6 Ms. inserts gloss: “that is, Kristos.” 7 Lit. “immediately.” 8 Apparently her house was outside the city. everything which I had done – he will be Mashiach!”
Then they went out of the city, and came to him.
(Now in the meantime his talmidim had entreated him that he should eat.
But he said to them, “I am about to eat something that you do not know of.”
So the talmidim said, “Is there someone who brought him something to eat?”
Then Yeshua said to them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me, in order that I can fulfill his work.
Do you not say that there are four months from now until the time of the harvest? Behold, I say to you: lift up your eyes, and see that the crops of the harvest are white already.
[And he who gathers, hires you, and gathers fruit according to your everlasting life] – in order that he who sows and he who gathers may be glad together.
For in this case the word is true that, ‘it is one who sows, and another who gathers.’
I, I am sending you to gather that which you have not burdened in. Others are they who burdened over it, but you, you are entering into the labor of their hand.”)
Many Shomronim of that city believed in him because of the words of the woman who did witness of him – that he told her everything she had done.
So when the Shomronim had come unto him, they entreated him that he should stay there with them, so he stayed two days.

And even more people believed in him through his words; 4 and they said to the woman, “We do not believe through your words; but we ourselves, we heard him and know that this is in truth the Savior of the world!” 1 Or possibly “he himself is Mashiach.” 2 Or “perform.” 3 Lit. “it is a true word…” 4 Or “because of.”
After two days he [departed] from there and went into Gelilah.
And he gave witness that no prophet has honor in his own land.
Then, when Yeshua came into Gelilah, the Gelilim received him because they saw everything he did in Yerushalayim in the day of the Feast – when he came to the day of the Feast.
Then he came again in Beit-Gelilah,3 to the place where he had made wine out of water. Now there was a small king ( )4 there, who had a sick son in Kephar Nachum.
So when he heard that Yeshua came from Yehudah into Gelilah, he went unto him that he would come down to heal his son – for he was in danger to die.
Then Yeshua said unto him, “Will you not believe except you see signs and miracles?”
So the nobleman said unto him, “Adon,5 come down before my son dies!”
Yeshua said unto him, “Go, your son is alive!” And the man believed the word which Yeshua said to him, and went away.
So after he was content to go down, his servants came up to him, and told him that his son lived.
So he asked that they should tell him the time that the wellbeing returned to him, and they said to him, “Yesterday, in the seventh hour of the day the fever left him.”
Then the father realized that that was the hour when Yeshua told him that his son was alive; and all his household believed in him.

This was 1 Or “testified.” 2 Hebrew "( "מועדmo’ed) Lit. “appointed time ”. 3 Lit. ‘house of Galilee.’ 4 Ms. inserts gloss: ‘nobleman.’ 5 Hebrew word for ‘Master.’ 6 Or “wanted,” could also mean “when he went down willingly.” 7 Lit. “his good strength.” the second sign which Yeshua did in Beit-Gelilah, when he came from Yehudah.
